items.context: Cook's first dissent since joining the Board in 2022; first time since 1992 a governor and a bank president dissent together. Warsh declines forward guidance and says politics played no role. September CPI 3.7% year on year; December hike was about 78% priced before the vote (CME FedWatch via Fortune).
items.fxnote: Provisional: the Warsh-led Board held and Cook voted to hike, which keeps rate control with the Board and weakens the Maximalists' case against Cook; re-score if the Nov 5 hearing or a December cut/hike reverses that.
items.rationale: Net effect (my reading): the Board, not the White House, keeps the rate decision, and its pull is toward tightening, so Trump's push for cuts gets no traction before the election while a December hike stays likely. Cook voting to hike undercuts the picture of her as a Trump-opposed dove, which complicates the Maximalists' Nov 5 case; the hold itself (not a hike) is the Warsh-led majority waiting. Counter-reading: a hold with two hawkish dissents may be Warsh buying time until after Nov 3, so the December hike is not locked. Falsifier: Warsh signals a cut or the Board splits the other way. Tags left empty because no faction clearly gained or lost; the effect falls on the Board and the administration's rate goals. Vote details are consistent across two read sources; Axios and CNBC pages could not be fetched.
items.source: Fortune, 404K Research (Warsh press conference), Axios and CNBC headlines

items.context: Background: Trump wants to remove Cook, a Biden appointee, for cause over mortgage-fraud allegations she denies; courts have kept her seat, and on Oct 9 the White House set up its own committee hearing as a new route to removal. The delay means Cook votes at the Dec 8-9 meeting, where a hike is priced; she dissented for a hike in October. November 6 follow-up: Reuters reports Hassett indicated December 14 for the hearing; the joint court status report says the parties are still discussing process. Cook’s counsel seeks neutrality and evidence disclosure before participation. https://www.investing.com/news/politics-news/feds-cook-lawyer-seeks-clarity-ahead-of-any-white-house-hearing-5006076
items.fxnote: No fx: a scheduling delay Cook's side asked for; neither the removal effort nor her seat changed.
items.rationale: My reading: the reported December 14 date keeps the planned hearing after the December 8–9 rate meeting. Participation and procedural fairness remain contested; neither removal nor a new court ruling is established.
